children: By Rodrigo Campos
A gauge of global stocks fell in choppy trading on Wednesday after Nvidia's quarterly results and ahead of Anthropic's market debut, while the dollar's strength also weighed on sentiment.

The dollar strengthened to a fresh 19-month high after US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC the central bank needs to either approve a half-point interest rate hike at its December meeting or communicate a faster pace of hikes in 2027.
Mining stocks dragged European shares lower, while Nvidia's results initially helped Asian shares, with Korea's Kospi
up 2% overnight. But the Nvidia rally fizzled and the stock was down 2.4% after rising as much as 2.7%.
Nvidia's board dismissed the idea of rehiring former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week. The company forecast sales ahead of Wall Street targets on Tuesday.

"The central question Nvidia faces is not related to this earnings report ... it's more about what the company may look like in 3-5 years without a visionary leader like Jensen and as competition from other chipmakers takes shape," said Jay Peters, portfolio manager at NewEdge Wealth.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average
CBOE:SPX
eased 0.07% to 7,335.43 and the Nasdaq Composite
MSCI's gauge of global stocks
EURONEXT:IACWI
fell 0.34% to 1,075.82 and the pan-European STOXX 600
index dropped 1.03%. Emerging market stocks
CBOE:EFS
eased 0.13% and Japan's Nikkei
rose 0.28%.
The next health check on the AI industry will come as Anthropic prepares to price its shares on Wednesday ahead of its market debut.
DOLLAR UP, OIL DOWN
In currencies, the dollar strengthened as Waller's comments and recent economic data cemented expectations for an interest rate hike next month.

"The Federal Reserve seems at the moment to be very determined to hike interest rates and maybe even aggressively do so," said Juan Perez, senior director of trading at Monex USA in Washington. "That's the belief right now that's carrying the US dollar."
The dollar index rose 0.19% to 103.81, with the euro
In commodities markets, crude prices fell after US crude and fuel inventories rose more than expected, adding to expectations of a supply surplus.
US crude
fell 4.39% to $82.23 a barrel and Brent
dropped to $90.93 per barrel, down 2.37%.
Spot gold
fell 2.86% to $3,739.66 an ounce and spot silver
lost 4.72% to $45.16 an ounce. Copper
declined 4.69% to $12,606.00 a ton.
US Treasury yields were slightly lower as oil prices dropped, dragging inflation expectations lower.
The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes
fell 3.87 basis points to 5.064% from 5.103% late on Tuesday, while the 30-year bond (US30YT=RR) yield fell 4.49 basis points to 5.414% from 5.459%.
